post.instagram_caption:
The first text message ever sent was two words: Merry Christmas.

Vodafone engineer Neil Papworth sent it on December 3, 1992, and he typed it on a computer, not a phone. It arrived on an Orbitel phone that weighed about 2 kg (Reuters, Euronews).

In December 2021, Vodafone auctioned that same message as an NFT in Paris. It sold for €107,000, about $121,000, and the money went to UNHCR, the UN refugee agency (Reuters).

The lesson: some of the biggest habits in tech started as a tiny test.

Source: Reuters, Euronews, City AM, Dec 21, 2021.

The first text message, "Merry Christmas", was sent on December 3, 1992 by Vodafone engineer Neil Papworth, typed on a computer and received on an Orbitel phone that weighed about 2 kg. In 2021 Vodafone auctioned it as an NFT in Paris for €107,000, about $121,000, for the UN refugee agency.
